There is a version of Christianity circulating right now that has made its peace with Darwin. It calls itself humble. It calls the people who disagree with it naive, fearful, and unable to handle complexity. It speaks of deeper readings and the living voice of Christ rising above the crude surface of the text. It posts about chromosome 2 and calls that faith.

This is not a new faith. It is an old capitulation dressed in new vocabulary.

Pull the thread and see what comes with it.

What the Theistic Evolutionist Does With Romans 5

Take the best-case version of evolution as given. The theistic evolutionist still has a problem that no deeper reading resolves. It is not a surface problem. It is a bone-deep contradiction.

Paul’s entire account of redemption stands on a single hinge. Romans 5:12: through one man sin entered the world, and death through sin.

“Therefore, just as through one man sin entered the world, and death through sin, and thus death passed to all men, because all sinned.”

This is the hinge the entire redemption account turns on. Christ is the second Adam precisely because the first Adam introduced something real that required real undoing.

Evolution requires death before Adam. Not symbolic death. Biological death. Millions of years of predation, extinction, suffering, and decay, all prior to any human sin, all built into creation itself. On the evolutionary account, death is not the consequence of the Fall. Death is the foundation the creation was built on.

Which means the Cross redeems something that was never broken. The second Adam fixes a problem the first Adam did not cause. Redemption becomes a category error. The entire weight of Paul’s argument dissolves.

Every theistic evolutionist has quietly let Romans 5 go. They keep the vocabulary, sin, redemption, the Cross, while gutting the ground those words stand on. This is not depth. This is a body without bones, standing upright by borrowed memory.

The Image That Cannot Emerge Gradually

Genesis 1:26:

“And God said, Let Us make man according to Our image and likeness, and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the flying creatures of heaven, and over the cattle and all the earth, and over all the reptiles that creep on the earth.”

Man is made in the image of God. This is not incidental language. It is the anthropological foundation beneath every ethic, every law, every claim about human dignity that exists in the record, including the claims secular culture still borrows without crediting their source.

If man emerged gradually from earlier hominids through blind selection, then at what generation did the image appear?

Was Homo erectus image-bearing? Was Homo habilis? Was there a father who was not image-bearing and a son who was? Did God breathe the image into a primate mid-sequence, and if so, what was the primate before the breath?

Every answer produces a horror. Either the image is a biological accident that selection pressure happened to produce, which destroys its authority entirely, or God presided over millions of years of almost-image-bearers, creatures who almost had dignity, almost counted, almost mattered, before the threshold was crossed by accident of genetic drift.

That is not the God of the text. That is a different God wearing the same name.

The image cannot emerge gradually. It either is or it is not. The moment you introduce gradualism into the anthropology, you have not deepened your theology. You have replaced it.

The Institution You’re Being Asked to Trust

One observation about the knowledge class asking for your deference.

This is the same institution that kept Ernst Haeckel’s fraudulent embryo drawings, falsified illustrations used to certify common descent in biology textbooks for over a century after colleagues identified the manipulations the year they were published. The same institution that received a composite forgery as the missing link between ape and man: human cranium, orangutan jaw, teeth filed to pass for human, the whole assembly chemically stained to simulate age. Forty years of research built on it. The exposure absorbed without consequence.

False evidence certifying the central conclusion, dissent quietly punished, the consensus rolling forward unchanged once the embarrassment passed.

Real data exists. The point is narrower: you are being asked to place the weight of your theological anthropology on the confident pronouncements of a knowledge class with a documented history of managing narrative rather than pursuing truth. That history doesn’t exonerate the institution. It disqualifies it from the deference it demands.

The Hermeneutic That Only Activates on Cue

The theistic evolutionist will tell you that the literalist is afraid of depth. That it takes courage to move beyond the surface. That the living voice of Christ transcends the written text.

Then he will tell you that the genetic similarity evidence is overwhelming and should be accepted directly. No depth needed there. No courage required. The surface is fine when the surface agrees with the academy.

The deeper reading hermeneutic does not activate randomly. It activates at the precise points where the text resists the secular consensus. Romans 5 needs depth. Genesis 1 needs courage. The fossil record does not. The genomic data does not.

This is not a hermeneutic. It is a hierarchy. The secular academy sits at the top. The text gets interpreted upward toward that ceiling, never downward toward its own root.

Constantine did not destroy the early church with persecution. He destroyed it with patronage. The academy does the same thing with credentialing. You do not need to burn the text. You need to make the people who hold it plainly feel ashamed of holding it plainly. That is the oldest move in the record.

And it is working.

What the Text Actually Requires

The Cross requires a real Adam. A real Fall. A real introduction of death into a creation that did not contain it before. A real image-bearing that cannot be arrived at by selection pressure across millions of years of predation and extinction.

These are not incidental details awaiting a more sophisticated reading. They are the bones the redemption narrative stands on. Remove them and you do not have a deeper Christianity. You have a Christianity-shaped void, the vocabulary preserved, the bones gone.

The wider canon makes this harder to escape, not easier. Jubilees 2 gives the precise account of a created order with a designed calendar and a specific anthropology written into the bone before Sinai. The Book of Enoch gives the account of a cosmic order intact before the Watchers corrupted it. You cannot corrupt what evolution built through corruption. You cannot restore through redemption what selection pressure produced by accident. The 81-book canon does not soften the contradiction. It sharpens it.

The theistic evolutionist wants a faith capacious enough to hold Darwin and the Cross simultaneously. The Cross will not hold that weight. It was not built to redeem a creation that death designed. It was built to reverse a death that sin introduced, through one man, into a world that did not have it before.

That is either true or the Cross means nothing.

There is no deeper reading that resolves this. There is only the choice between the text and the academy, and the honesty to name which one you are actually standing on.

Your image-bearing is not a biological accident. It was spoken before the foundations of the world.
